scope: Official primary NVIDIA, Vulkan loader, Chromium Linux sandbox, and Linux process-access sources; no live GPU execution

sources.title: NVIDIA Linux x86_64 driver 580.159.03 official download directory
sources.verifiedFact: The exact driver release is present in NVIDIA's official distribution, with .run entries dated 2026-04-24.
sources.projectRelevance: Confirms the historical successful driver version exists. Does not identify the latest failed host driver.
sources.limitation: Directory modification date is not asserted as a product release-note publication date.

sources.title: NVIDIA 580.159.03 README: Installed Components
sources.verifiedFact: libGLX_nvidia.so.0 and libEGL_nvidia.so.0 can serve as Vulkan ICDs. The default ICD refers to libGLX_nvidia.so.0; the README discusses libEGL_nvidia.so.0 when X11 client libraries are unavailable.
sources.projectRelevance: Historical successful ICD libGLX_nvidia.so.0 is valid, not itself a fault. Loader dependencies and actual resolved libraries are distinguishing evidence.
sources.limitation: No missing X11 library, mismatched NVIDIA library, or broken symlink has been observed in the latest job.

sources.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit: Specialized Configurations with Docker
sources.version: Latest documentation; includes 1.20.0 behavior notes; deployed host Toolkit version unknown
sources.verifiedFact: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES selects injected driver capabilities. utility supports NVML/nvidia-smi; graphics supports OpenGL/EGL/Vulkan. all requests all available capabilities.
sources.projectRelevance: nvidia-smi recognition does not prove graphics initialization. The historical all setting is intent, not proof of current injection success.
sources.limitation: Current docs' CDI/JIT-CDI changes must not be assumed on a host with unrecorded Toolkit version and runtime mode.

sources.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit source: graphics discoverer
sources.version: Current main source observed 2026-11-01; not the identified deployed host version
sources.verifiedFact: The Toolkit discovers graphics libraries, EGL vendor manifests, Vulkan ICD manifests, and related symlink hooks for container injection.
sources.projectRelevance: Immutable application image identity alone does not establish host-injected graphics-driver identity.
sources.limitation: Explains architecture, not proof of a missing mount in gCube.

sources.title: Khronos Vulkan Loader: Driver Interface
sources.version: Current primary documentation; some loader environment features have explicit Vulkan-header minimums
sources.verifiedFact: VK_DRIVER_FILES supersedes VK_ICD_FILENAMES; otherwise standard discovery applies. Discovery of an ICD JSON does not guarantee resolution of its shared library. Elevated-privilege security contexts can ignore override variables and user paths.
sources.projectRelevance: Historical VK_ICD_FILENAMES=null is compatible with successful default discovery. The capture allowlist excludes newer override and XDG search variables, a conditional difference from health/host environments.
sources.limitation: The omitted variables are not known to have been set or required during the latest failed job. UID0 alone is not used as proof of secure execution.

sources.title: Khronos Vulkan Loader: Loader Interface Architecture
sources.version: Current primary documentation; VK_DRIVER_FILES requires loaders built with Vulkan headers 1.3.207 or newer
sources.verifiedFact: Security-sensitive environment handling uses secure_getenv or platform-equivalent checks; elevated-privilege contexts can suppress environment overrides.
sources.projectRelevance: Root health and UID1000 capture require matching effective launch conditions before comparing Vulkan results.
sources.limitation: No AT_SECURE, setuid transition, file-capability, or effective loader behavior was collected from the latest capture process.

sources.title: Chromium Linux Sandboxing
sources.version: Pinned documentation commit 0b6120702e8f69ce43b34b02903a1d32a0be07d3; generic Linux architecture, not an exact Chromium155 regression report
sources.verifiedFact: Linux Chromium uses namespace and seccomp sandbox layers; the GPU process uses seccomp-BPF.
sources.projectRelevance: Actual nonroot sandboxed capture and root no-sandbox health are different execution conditions.
sources.limitation: No sandbox denial, fatal namespace error, or matching Chromium155 defect is established. No sandbox bypass is recommended.

sources.title: Linux man-pages: proc_pid_environ(5)
sources.verifiedFact: /proc/PID/environ exposes the initial exec environment, not necessarily later modifications. Access is governed by PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS.
sources.projectRelevance: Diagnostic v1 reading another process's environ is not equivalent to Studio passing its own filtered environment. Generic launcher failure does not prove a renderer failure.
sources.limitation: The v1 response lacks the failed stage, exception class and errno; permission failure remains a hypothesis. No full environment dump is requested.

sources.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit: Troubleshooting
sources.version: Latest primary documentation; applicability depends on installed Toolkit/runtime/cgroup mode
sources.verifiedFact: Documents conditional GPU device-access loss after container/runtime updates in legacy hook/cgroup configurations, including NVML Unknown Error symptoms; also documents distinct SELinux access errors.
sources.projectRelevance: Provider-side device access can vary independently of application image contents.
sources.limitation: No same-job NVML Unknown Error, SELinux denial, daemon reload, or matching runtime mode was observed; these are conditional mechanisms, not the confirmed WebGL2 cause.

sources.title: NVIDIA 580.159.03 README: Known Issues
sources.verifiedFact: Vulkan device enumeration/presentation restrictions described depend on X server and X.Org version. Administrative restrictions on GPU performance counters are a separate feature.
sources.projectRelevance: Provides conditions for excluding blanket X-server and administrative-privilege prescriptions.
sources.limitation: No current X-server condition or performance-counter use was demonstrated. Neither issue is established as the capture failure.
